subject.title: fix(cron): pin the cron webhook bearer token to operator-allowlisted hosts

question: Should upgrades with an existing `cron.webhookToken` and no `cron.webhookTokenHosts` fail closed by withholding bearer authentication, or preserve existing authentication until the operator explicitly opts into host pinning?
rationale: The patch correctly implements either localized behavior, but selecting the default trades an active secret-exfiltration boundary against a breaking change to established webhook integrations; that policy cannot be settled mechanically.

options.title: Approve fail-closed rollout
options.body: Keep the proposed empty-allowlist denial and Doctor advisory so untrusted job destinations cannot receive the token by default after upgrade.

options.title: Preserve legacy delivery by default
options.body: Treat an absent allowlist as legacy attach-everywhere behavior and require a separately chosen strict mode, accepting that the reported leak remains possible by default.

options.title: Pause for a narrower migration design
options.body: Defer merge until maintainers define an upgrade mechanism that does not silently break existing receivers or automatically trust agent-controlled job destinations.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed rollout
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed empty-allowlist denial and Doctor advisory so untrusted job destinations cannot receive the token by default after upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied evidence identifies this contributor as the only concrete person connected to the current implementation; final security-policy ownership remains to be assigned by the repository.
